subject: math
intro: This cluster test covers displaying numerical data in dot plots, histograms, and box plots (6.SP.B.4) and summarizing numerical data sets with measures of center and spread (6.SP.B.5). Choose the single best answer for each multiple-choice item.

items.prompt:
A dot plot of the number of books read shows $3$ dots above $0$, $4$ dots above $1$, $2$ dots above $2$, and $1$ dot above $4$. How many students are represented in all?
A) $4$
B) $7$
C) $10$
D) $13$

steps: Each dot represents one student, so add the number of dots: $3 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10$.
There are $10$ students in all.
A) $4$ counts only the distinct values that have dots ($0, 1, 2, 4$), not the total number of dots.
B) $7$ and D) $13$ are partial or incorrect sums of the dot counts.

items.prompt:
A histogram of test scores has intervals $50\text{–}59$ (height $2$), $60\text{–}69$ (height $5$), $70\text{–}79$ (height $8$), $80\text{–}89$ (height $4$), and $90\text{–}99$ (height $1$). How many students scored at least $70$?
A) $8$
B) $12$
C) $13$
D) $20$

steps: Scores of at least $70$ fall in the intervals $70\text{–}79$, $80\text{–}89$, and $90\text{–}99$.
Add the bar heights for those intervals: $8 + 4 + 1 = 13$.
A) $8$ uses only the $70\text{–}79$ interval and forgets the higher intervals.
B) $12$ leaves out the $90\text{–}99$ interval, and D) $20$ adds every interval, including those below $70$.

items.prompt:
A box plot of quiz scores shows $\min = 4$, $Q_1 = 7$, median $= 10$, $Q_3 = 13$, and $\max = 18$. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
A) $3$
B) $6$
C) $9$
D) $14$

steps: The IQR is the difference of the upper and lower quartiles: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
A) $3$ uses only median $- Q_1 = 10 - 7$, not the full IQR.
C) $9$ and D) $14$ come from $\max - \min$ type computations ($18 - 9$ or $18 - 4$), which give the range, not the IQR.

items.prompt:
Plant heights in centimeters are $4, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 18, 19, 21, 23$. Using equal-width intervals of width $5$ starting at $0$ ($0\text{–}4$, $5\text{–}9$, $10\text{–}14$, $15\text{–}19$, $20\text{–}24$), what is the frequency (bar height) of the $10\text{–}14$ interval?
A) $2$
B) $3$
C) $4$
D) $5$

steps: List the values that fall in $10\text{–}14$ (at least $10$ and at most $14$): $11, 12, 14$.
That is $3$ values, so the bar height for $10\text{–}14$ is $3$.
A) $2$ misses one value, and C) $4$, D) $5$ include values from neighboring intervals such as $9$ or $18$.
Equal-width contiguous bins mean each height is just a count of the values landing in that interval.

items.prompt:
Order the data $7, 3, 9, 5, 11, 8, 6$ and find the median.
A) $7$
B) $8$
C) $9$
D) $11$

steps: First order the data: $3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11$.
With $n = 7$ values, the median is the $4$th value (the middle position).
The $4$th ordered value is $7$, so the median is $7$.
B) $8$ and C) $9$ take the middle of the unordered list or the wrong position; D) $11$ is the maximum, not the median.

items.prompt:
You want to show how $200$ commute times group into ranges such as $0\text{–}9$, $10\text{–}19$, and so on, without listing every individual time. Which display is most appropriate?
A) A dot plot, with one dot per commute time
B) A histogram, with a bar for each range of times
C) A box plot, showing every individual commute time
D) A circle (pie) graph of the exact times
items.answer: B) A histogram, with a bar for each range of times

steps: A histogram groups numerical data into equal-width intervals and shows the frequency in each range, which is exactly what is asked.
A) A dot plot would need $200$ individual dots and does not group values into ranges cleanly.
C) A box plot summarizes with a five-number summary; it does not show individual times, and the prompt's claim that it shows every value is false.
D) A circle graph shows parts of a whole for categories, not ranges of a numerical variable.
solution.answer: B) A histogram, with a bar for each range of times

items.prompt:
A list gives the daily high temperature in degrees Fahrenheit for one week: $68, 71, 65, 70, 73, 69, 72$. How many observations are in this data set?
A) $5$
B) $6$
C) $7$
D) $8$

steps: The number of observations $n$ is simply the count of values in the list.
Counting $68, 71, 65, 70, 73, 69, 72$ gives $7$ values.
So $n = 7$ observations of daily high temperature.
A) $5$, B) $6$, and D) $8$ miscount the entries in the list.

items.prompt:
Find the mean of the data set $4, 7, 7, 9, 13$.
A) $7$
B) $8$
C) $9$
D) $13$

steps: The mean is the sum of the values divided by how many there are: $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x_i}{n}$.
Add the values: $4 + 7 + 7 + 9 + 13 = 40$.
Divide by $n = 5$: $\bar{x} = \frac{40}{5} = 8$.
A) $7$ is the median or mode, not the mean; C) $9$ and D) $13$ are single data values, not the average.

items.prompt:
For the data set $3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 15, 18$, what is the range?
A) $12$
B) $15$
C) $18$
D) $21$

steps: The range is the maximum minus the minimum: $\text{range} = \max - \min$.
Here $\max = 18$ and $\min = 3$, so $\text{range} = 18 - 3 = 15$.
A) $12$ is one of the data values, not the spread; C) $18$ is just the maximum.
D) $21$ comes from adding $\max + \min = 18 + 3$ instead of subtracting.

items.prompt:
Find the median of the data set $4, 9, 7, 7, 13, 11$.
A) $7$
B) $8$
C) $9$
D) $10$

steps: First order the data: $4, 7, 7, 9, 11, 13$.
With $n = 6$ (an even count), the median is the average of the two middle values, the $3$rd and $4$th: $7$ and $9$.
A) $7$ takes a single middle value without averaging (or uses the unsorted list); C) $9$ uses only the upper middle value; D) $10$ is the midpoint of $7$ and $13$, the wrong pair.

items.prompt:
Compute the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the data set $2, 4, 6, 8$.
A) $0$
B) $2$
C) $\frac{8}{3}$
D) $5$

steps: First find the mean: $\bar{x} = \frac{2 + 4 + 6 + 8}{4} = \frac{20}{4} = 5$.
Find the absolute deviation of each value from the mean: $|2-5| = 3$, $|4-5| = 1$, $|6-5| = 1$, $|8-5| = 3$.
Average those deviations: $\text{MAD} = \frac{3 + 1 + 1 + 3}{4} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$.
A) $0$ comes from forgetting the absolute value so the signed deviations cancel; C) $\frac{8}{3}$ divides by $n-1 = 3$ instead of $n = 4$; D) $5$ is the mean, not the MAD.

items.prompt:
House prices on a street are $\$210{,}000$, $\$220{,}000$, $\$230{,}000$, $\$240{,}000$, and $\$900{,}000$. Which measure of center better summarizes a typical price, and why?
A) The mean, because it uses every value
B) The median, because the single very large price pulls the mean up and makes it higher than most homes
C) The mean, because it equals the most common price
D) The median, because it is always larger than the mean
items.answer: B) The median, because the single very large price pulls the mean up and makes it higher than most homes

steps: The median is the middle of the ordered values, $\$230{,}000$, which is close to four of the five prices.
The single outlier $\$900{,}000$ inflates the mean to $\$360{,}000$, higher than every home except the outlier, so the median is more typical.
A) and C) keep the mean despite the outlier distortion; D) gives a false reason, since the median is not always larger than the mean.
solution.answer: B) The median, because the single very large price pulls the mean up and makes it higher than most homes
